item.title: MLBB hero builds 2026: what players build in ranked
item.description: What players really build in ranked: builds for the ten most picked heroes, the most common items, emblems and battle spells.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
The most common core item is Dominance Ice: it is in the popular build of 24 heroes out of 133.

item.title: Who to ban in Mobile Legends: the most dangerous heroes by rank
item.description: Hirara is banned in two matches out of three yet wins half her games. We look at who really deserves your ban and who counters them if it is gone.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
Hirara is banned the most: in 67.97% of matches across all ranks and 86.38% in Mythical Glory.
Yet Hirara wins only 50.03% of matches. Masha (60.40% wins) and Marcel (57.46%) are more dangerous if left open.
Belerick is banned in 56.83% of matches across all ranks.
Strong heroes almost nobody bans: Valir (54.11% wins at 3.78% bans), Hanabi and Ling.

item.title: How to rank up solo in Mobile Legends: heroes and star maths
item.description: We work out how many matches each percent of wins costs, pick solo heroes for every lane and see who is strong in Epic and who in Mythical Glory.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
At a 50% win rate your stars stand still on average: every loss takes back what a win gave.
At 55% wins the road from Legend V to Mythic (25 stars) takes about 250 matches, at 60% about 125.
The best solo heroes in Legend and Mythic by MOONTON’s 30-day statistics: Minsitthar, Ling, Valir, Hanabi and Rafaela.
Belerick and Atlas win the most in Epic but fall to 50% by Mythical Glory. Saber and Moskov are the opposite: stronger at the top.
The solo hero data covers 30 days ending on 23 November 2026. The match estimates below assume a constant win rate.
How many matches 25 stars take
A win gives a star and a loss takes one. So on average a match earns your win share minus your loss share. At 55% that is 0.1 stars per game, and the 25 Legend stars turn into roughly 250 matches. The estimate is rough: star protection and promotion points in Epic and Legend speed things up a little, but the order of magnitude is right.

Which heroes are best for solo queue
We took heroes picked in at least 0.6% of matches and banned in less than 25% — the ones you can actually get in solo queue. Then we sorted them by win rate in Legend and Mythic, where most players get stuck.

A hero that is strong in Epic is not always strong in Glory
Some heroes’ win rates change a lot with rank. Easy-to-learn tanks win at the bottom, while in Mythical Glory players already know how to play against them. Mechanically demanding heroes go the other way.

What else helps you collect stars
Keep two or three heroes of one role plus a backup for a neighbouring lane. Your win rate is higher on a familiar hero than on a new one.
Learn your heroes’ counters: every hero page in our tier list shows the five heroes they lose to.
Stop after two losses in a row. A tilted streak usually costs more stars than it brings.
Do not spend ranked games on experiments: try a new hero in Classic first.
In Epic and Legend play for performance: good matches build promotion points, and a full star protection bar saves you from a loss.

item.title: Mobile Legends account: how to bind, switch and recover it
item.description: Why a guest profile disappears with your phone, which login is safest, how to open a second account, recover a lost one and delete one you no longer need.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
A guest account with no binding cannot be moved to another phone or restored after you delete the game. MOONTON’s terms say so directly.
You can bind the game to a Moonton account by email or to a Google, Apple ID, Facebook, TikTok or VK login.
Everything lives in the profile: Account → Account Center. That is where you bind, switch profiles, unbind social logins and delete.
If you do not log in for more than 6 months, MOONTON may delete the account along with its diamonds and skins.
Why a guest account is risky
If you have never bound your account, you are playing on a guest profile that lives only on your phone. MOONTON’s terms of 21 October 2025 say that guest progress cannot be transferred, purchases cannot be restored after a reinstall, and deleting the game wipes the data for good. MOONTON does not guarantee recovery of such an account and recommends creating a Moonton account or binding a third-party login.
Open your profile, then Account → Account Center. If no login method is marked as bound, you are on a guest profile. Bind at least one method before you change phones.
Check it now
How to bind your account
Tap the avatar in the top-left corner of the main screen.
Open Account and choose Account Center.
Pick a login method. A Moonton account needs a working email: you receive a code there, then set a password.
For Google, Apple ID, Facebook, TikTok or VK, sign in to that account and confirm access.
Go back to Account Center and check that the method is marked as bound.
Which login method to choose
Method
What you need
When it fits
Moonton account
Email and password
The main method: it does not depend on social networks or your phone
Google
A Google account
Android and moving from one Android phone to another
Apple ID
An Apple account
iPhone and iPad
Facebook, TikTok, VK
An active social account
A backup: if the social account is blocked or deleted, you cannot log in through it
It is safer to bind two methods at once: a Moonton account plus Google or Apple ID. ONE Esports, in its account security guide, also recommends relying on a Moonton account and unbinding extra third-party logins.
How to switch accounts or log in to a second one
A second profile is created on the same phone; you do not need to delete the game. Reinstalling does not help: on iPhone the game opens the old account again. Before switching, make sure your main account is bound, or you will not be able to return to it.
Open your profile, go to Account and tap the switch button (Switch Account in the English client).
Log in with the method bound to the other account, or register a new Moonton account with a different email.
To go back, tap Switch Account again and log in with the method bound to your main profile.
How to recover your account
Start simple: log in with the method the account was bound to. If logging in with Google or VK opens a new empty profile, that method is bound to a different account or there was no binding at all.
Log in with your Moonton account, Google, Apple ID, Facebook, TikTok or VK. A Moonton password is reset with a code sent to the bound email.
If nothing was bound, open Account Center and choose account recovery (Retrieve Account). AFK Gaming describes a check based on in-game details: the old account ID, server number and nickname.
If that fails, contact support from the game: the support icon is in your profile. Give your ID, the server number in brackets, nickname, roughly when the account was created and what you bought on it.
Sites and people who offer to recover or unban an account for money are scammers. Accounts are recovered only through the game and MOONTON support, and MOONTON never asks for your password for codes or gifts.
Be careful
How to delete your account
Deleting the game from your phone does not delete the account: a bound profile stays on MOONTON’s servers. According to the cyber.sports.ru guide, deletion takes two steps: in Account Center you unbind third-party logins and tap Delete Account, then the game opens play.mobilelegends.com, where you accept the agreements, log in and confirm with the Confirm to Cancel button.
The account is not deleted at once: the request waits up to 30 days, and logging in during that time offers a Give Up button that cancels the deletion.
After deletion your rank, heroes, skins and diamonds are gone. They cannot be restored.
According to cyber.sports.ru, the same email and social accounts cannot be bound to a new account afterwards.
A request to delete personal data under MOONTON’s privacy policy goes to dpo@moonton.com.
If you just want a clean profile, you do not have to delete the old one: create a second one with Switch Account.
What happens to an abandoned account
Under MOONTON’s terms an account nobody has logged in to for more than 6 months may be deleted or deactivated, and its diamonds and items are lost without compensation. If you have taken a break from the game, log in at least once every few months.

item.title: New MLBB heroes 2026: releases, revamps and what comes next
item.description: Hirara, Marcel, Sora and the Masha and Bruno revamps: release dates from patch notes, current win and ban rates and what is known about the next hero.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
The latest new hero is Hirara, a jungle assassin. She was released on 17 June 2026 with patch 2.1.88.
Since December 2025 three new heroes have come out: Sora, Marcel and Hirara. Four more were revamped: Eudora, Aulus, Masha and Bruno.
Hirara is banned in 68% of matches, the highest ban rate among all 133 heroes.
As of 22 November MOONTON has not announced the next hero. The latest official patch notes are 2.2.16 from 16 September.

When the next new hero comes out
In 2025 and 2026 new heroes arrived about once every three months: in June, September and December 2025, then in March and June 2026. Since Hirara there has been no new hero for five months. There is no official announcement as of 22 November, so we will not name a hero or a date: rumours about new heroes are often wrong.
As soon as MOONTON publishes patch notes with a new hero, we will update this article and its tables. The easiest place to follow announcements is the Patch section on the game's official site.

item.title: How to change your MLBB nickname: price, invisible name, symbols
item.description: We change the name in the profile, sort out the card price, build a blank nickname from Unicode characters and check that the game accepts it.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In brief
You change your nickname in the profile: tap the avatar in the top-left corner, then your name.
On a new account the first change is free. After that you need a Rename Card.
The card costs diamonds. Guides quote 239 and 299 diamonds, so check the exact price in the shop.
A blank nickname is built from invisible Unicode characters, but the game may reject them.
How to change your nickname: step by step
In the main menu, tap your avatar in the top-left corner. Your profile opens.
Tap your current nickname or the pencil icon next to it.
Type the new name. If it has symbols, put it together in your notes first and paste it in one go.
Tap OK. If you have not used the free change yet, the name changes without a card.
If the free change is gone, the game asks for a Rename Card. A card you bought can also be used from the backpack: find it among your items and tap Use.
Rank, stars, heroes, skins and statistics stay where they were after a rename. The account is identified by Game ID and Zone ID, not by the nickname, so your friends stay too: they simply see the new name.
How much a nickname change costs
Ways to change your nickname and their price
We found no official MOONTON price list. The figures come from guides by ONE Esports (May 2025) and aesthetic.name (October 2026).
Way
Price
Condition
First change
Free
Once per account, if you have never renamed
Rename Card from the shop
239 or 299 diamonds according to guides
The exact price is shown in the shop before you buy
Season first top-up quest
50 diamonds
According to ONE Esports: top up three times on different days
English guides find the card in the shop under the Special tab: ONE Esports gives the path Shop → Preparation → Special, aesthetic.name says Shop → Special → Items. MOONTON moves shop sections around from time to time, so it is quicker to open the shop and scroll through the item tabs.
Settle on the nickname first and check that it is free. If the name is taken or a symbol is not supported, the game shows an error and the name stays the same. Fix the name and try again; you do not need a second card for that.
Before you buy
How to make an invisible nickname
A blank name is not made with spaces but with characters that look empty while the game treats them as a letter or a sign. The two Unicode characters in the table below are the usual choice.
Characters for an invisible nickname
Copy what is inside the square brackets. On a phone it is easier to copy the character with the brackets, paste it into your notes and delete the brackets.
Character
Code
What it is
[ㅤ]
U+3164
Hangul Filler, an empty Korean letter
[⠀]
U+2800
Braille Pattern Blank, an empty Braille sign
Copy an empty character from the table.
Open the rename window in your profile and delete the old nickname.
Paste the character. If the game says the name is taken, add one or two more empty characters in a row or mix both kinds.
Tap OK and open your profile: the name should look empty.
There is no guarantee. The Indonesian outlet Katadata warned in November 2026 that not every blank character passes the check and that the rules can change with a game update. If one character is refused, try the other. Some players may see a box instead of an empty space.
Symbols and stylish nicknames
Besides Latin and Cyrillic letters, players often add hieroglyphs and decorative signs. Generator sites offer hundreds of options, but many of their "fonts" are made of rare Unicode characters: the game may refuse them or show boxes. One or two simple signs are the safer choice.
Signs players often put in a nickname
Paste the finished nickname into the rename field before buying a card. If a sign does not fit, the game tells you right away.
Sign

MOONTON does not officially state how many characters a nickname can have. The aesthetic.name guide gives 4 to 16 characters and warns that some signs count as two. It also mentions a 7 days pause between renames. We have not checked this ourselves, so go by the message the game shows.

item.title: MLBB redeem codes: where to enter them and why a code fails
item.description: Step-by-step redemption on the official MOONTON page, where to find your Game ID and Zone ID, why a code fails and how to spot a scam site.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
MLBB redeem codes are entered on the official page mobilelegends.com/redeem, not inside the game.
You need four fields: the code, your Game ID, Zone ID and a verification code sent to your in-game mail.
The verification code is valid for 30 minutes. The reward arrives in your in-game mail.
You never need your account password to redeem a code. A site that asks for it is a scam.
Where to enter a redeem code
Fields of the official form at mobilelegends.com/redeem
Field
What to enter
Where to find it
Redemption code
The code itself
From the official source that gave it out
Game ID
Your account number
In-game profile: the ID line next to your name
Zone ID
Your server number
Same place, the number in brackets after the Game ID
Verification Code
A confirmation code
Sent to your in-game mail after you press Send
How to redeem a code, step by step
Redeem a code
Mobile Legends
Open the form and enter the Game ID and Zone ID from your profile.
Open your in-game profile and note two numbers: the Game ID and the Zone ID in brackets, for example 123456789 (1234).
Go to mobilelegends.com/redeem and pick the site language if needed.
Paste the code into Redemption code, then enter your Game ID and Zone ID.
Press Send. Open your in-game mail: the verification code arrives there and is valid for 30 minutes.
Enter the verification code on the site and press Redeem. The reward arrives in your in-game mail.
The official form never asks for your password, email or Moonton ID details. If a “free diamonds” site asks you to log in, close it: that is how accounts get stolen.
Safety
Why a redeem code does not work
The code has expired. Every code has its own deadline, after which it is no longer accepted.
The code has run out. Many codes have a limited number of activations.
The code was already used on this account. The same code will not work twice.
The code is for another region or event. Some codes may work only on certain servers.
A typo in the Game ID or Zone ID. Check both numbers in your profile, especially the server number in brackets.
The verification code is stale. If more than 30 minutes have passed, press Send again.
Where to find real redeem codes
MOONTON hands out real codes itself: in the game’s official communities, during major tournaments and at special events. If a code appears on a list site without a link to its source, check the date and never enter it anywhere except mobilelegends.com/redeem. Services that “generate” codes or diamonds do not exist.
We do not publish code lists: a code cannot be checked without redeeming it on your own account, and outdated lists only waste time. If MOONTON releases a code for all players, we will cover it in the news with a link to the source.

item.title: Current MLBB patch: update 2.2.16 and what it changed
item.description: The key points of patch 2.2.16: the new Masha and Bruno, buffs and nerfs, match economy, the 2026 map and what happened to heroes two months later.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
The current MLBB patch is 2.2.16. It came out on 16 September 2026 together with the start of Season 42.
For the game’s 10th anniversary Masha and Bruno were reworked, and six more heroes got new models: Paquito, Kadita, Clint, Luo Yi, Brody and Badang.
Aulus, Argus, Aldous and Lukas were buffed; Miya, Hanabi, Melissa, Yi Sun-shin and Paquito were nerfed.
The next major patch is expected with Season 43: the last two arrived on the first day of a season, 17 June and 16 September.
Patch 2.2.16 changed how Masha and Bruno play. Lower jungle monster rewards slowed gold income.
What the patch did to heroes, two months on

The rework landed harder than expected: Masha now has the highest win rate in the game at 60.47%. Argus climbed to 56.76% after his buff. Hanabi was nerfed but is still the most picked hero and wins 52.64%. Tigreal got a shorter cooldown on his second skill, yet his win rate remains one of the lowest at 45.20%.
The new Masha and the new Bruno
Masha is now a berserker fighter built for long fights rather than an assassin for split-pushing. She still has three HP bars, and attacking from the side of the wound she left triggers Feral: three wide claw strikes plus Resilience, Attack Speed and Movement Speed.
Masha’s second skill resets its cooldown each time she loses one of her lives.
Bruno keeps his ball-kicking marksman style, but the ball is easier to control: its distance scales with Movement Speed, it stays on the ground for 3 seconds instead of 2 and no longer crosses walls.
Bruno’s ultimate now briefly stuns the first target, slows it heavily and knocks it back to his attack range.
Match economy and the 2026 map
Gold from the Horned Lizard, Fire Beetle and Lava Golem is down 13%.
The comeback kill bounty now triggers at a 1500 gold deficit instead of 2000.
Minion gold grows a little more slowly over time.
Since 28 September the annual map update is live: vision wisps reveal hidden enemies, the Turtle spawns an allied turtle on a lane instead of a shield, and destroying turrets gives the whole team much more gold.
MOONTON says matches were too fast and teams that fell behind struggled to come back. In ranked this means a gold lead is less safe: games more often go the distance, and late-game mistakes cost more.
What it means in ranked
Modes, season and other changes
VS A.I. and Custom matches unlock at Elite rank, Magic Chess at level 12 and 1 VS 1 at level 25.
A Multiplayer Training Camp was added: Mode — VS A.I. & Custom — Multiplayer Training Camp.
The player Namecard was reworked: you can show a 3D hero model and arrange cards with your Mythic medal, collection and achievements.
The Season 42 skin is Flamehide Thane for Popol and Kupa, and the avatar border is Starward Decade.
When the next patch comes out
The last two major updates, 2.1.88 (17 June) and 2.2.16 (16 September), arrived on the day a new season started. Season 42 is expected to end on 16 December, so the next big patch will most likely come then. There is no official date yet. Once it is out, we will update this guide and the hero tier list.

item.title: Mobile Legends ranks in order: all tiers, stars and Mythic
item.description: A table of every MLBB rank in order, how many stars it takes to reach Mythic, how Mythic ranks work, placement and star protection.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
Mobile Legends has 10 ranks: Warrior, Elite, Master, Grandmaster, Epic, Legend, Mythic, Mythical Honor, Mythical Glory and Mythical Immortal.
You need 112 stars to reach Mythic, most of them in Grandmaster, Epic and Legend — 25 each.
Mythic has no divisions: Honor starts at 25 stars, Glory at 50 and Immortal at 100.
The first 10 Mythic matches are placement: a win gives two stars and a loss removes none.
Before Mythic, divisions run from III or V to I. Each takes 3 to 5 stars. In Mythic, all stars go towards one total.

The first ranks are the shortest: Warrior takes 9 stars and Elite 12. The real work starts in Grandmaster: three ranks in a row with 25 stars each, and that is where new players most often get stuck.
Mythic ranks and placement
After Legend I the next win takes you to Mythic. Placement starts here: 10 matches where every win gives two stars and a loss takes none. After that stars again change by one per win or loss.

Stars add up with no cap
Out of 2,289 orders BOOST MLBB has completed since November 2025, 569 were stars inside Mythical Immortal and 343 inside Mythical Glory. The most common route between ranks is Glory to Immortal: 179 orders.
Where our customers play
How stars are gained and lost
A ranked win adds one star and a loss removes one.
The star protection bar fills up when you play well. When it is full, your next loss does not cost a star.
In Epic and Legend good matches also build star raising points: when the bar fills, you get an extra star.
In Mythic placement a win gives two stars, and a loss uses a match but removes no stars.
How many matches it takes to reach Mythic
Win rate decides everything. At 50% wins your stars barely move: losses cancel the wins, and only star protection pushes you forward. Every extra five percent of wins cuts the road several times. We estimated the number of matches including star protection and placement.
Approximate matches at different win rates
Assumptions: star protection triggers about once in six losses, and star raising points give a star every 35–50 matches. This is an estimate, not a game rule.

What happens to your rank at season end
A season lasts about three months. At the end your rank drops: Mythical Immortal and Mythical Glory start the new season in Legend V, Mythical Honor in Epic I and Mythic in Epic II. Rewards follow the highest rank you reached that season. We covered the expected end of Season 42 and the full reset chart in a separate guide.

item.title: When MLBB Season 42 ends and where your rank drops after the reset
item.description: The expected end of Season 42, the rank reset chart, season rewards and what happens to orders in the first days of a new season.
item.dc:creator: Boost MLBB Editorial Team
item.yandex:full-text:
In short
Season 42 is expected to end on 16 December 2026. Moonton has not announced the date in advance; it is estimated from past season lengths.
At the reset Mythical Immortal and Mythical Glory drop to Legend V, Mythical Honor to Epic I and Mythic to Epic II.
Season rewards follow the highest rank you reached during the season, not your rank on the last day.
To get the season skin you need to play 20 ranked matches.
The season started on 16 September. The 16 December estimate is based on previous seasons lasting about 91 days. Check the ranked mode timer for the in-game countdown.
When Season 42 ends
What is known about Season 42 and 43 timing as of 22 November 2026
Season 41 lasted 91 days. If Moonton announces a different time, we will update the table.

Usual season length

Average length of recent seasons
Season length varies: Season 40 ran for 98 days and Season 39 for 84 days. MOONTON ran the last changeover like this: Season 41 closed on 15 September at 21:59:59 server time, and Season 42 opened on 16 September at 00:00:00. So do not leave your last stars for 15 December. If the in-game timer shows a different date, trust the timer.
Where your rank drops after the reset
Rank reset at the start of a new season

Immortal and Glory players lose the most: hundreds of stars turn into Legend V. The way back is shorter than it looks: 25 Legend stars and Mythic placement, where a win in the first 10 matches gives two stars. Below Legend the reset is softer — Epic drops one or two divisions, and Warrior and Elite do not drop.
Which rewards a season gives
The reward follows the highest rank you reached during the season. If you were Mythic and fell back to Legend, you still get the Mythic reward.
The Season 42 skin is Flamehide Thane for Popol and Kupa. It requires 20 ranked matches.
Battle Points and tickets are given at every rank, and the amount grows with the rank.
The first week of a new season is the busiest. In the week Season 42 started, BOOST MLBB customers placed 102 orders against 30–40 in a normal summer week. Season 41 looked the same: 67 orders in its first week. Players want their rank back fast, and fewer boosters are free on those days.
What we see after every reset
What to do before the season ends
Open ranked mode and check the timer: the in-game date beats any forecast.
If you are a few stars short of the next rank, get them before 15 December — the reward follows your highest rank.
Finish 20 ranked matches if you have not yet and want the season skin.
If you plan a boost after the reset, order on the first day: the queue grows after that.
How stars, divisions and Mythic thresholds work is covered in our separate guide to Mobile Legends ranks in order. It also shows how many matches the road to Mythic usually takes at different win rates.
